page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the t2a server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache resources consist of 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This server does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across several multi-threaded and memory-bound workloads. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests register average scores of 1812.89 and 14472.4 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only small block speed of 563.91 GB/sec, which drops to 87.42 GB/sec for large blocks, alongside a write speed of 47.24 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks show mixed results; while gzip compression achieves an average throughput of 24.03 GB/sec, bzip3 decompression is weak at 8.58 GB/sec. Geekbench scores reflect a weak single-core performance of 1073.0 but an average multi-core score of 6000.0, supported by average results in software compilation and ray tracing.

The t2a-standard-8 demonstrates specific hardware tradeoffs, particularly in cryptographic and vector processing tasks. The Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor supports AES cryptography but lacks advanced vector extensions and advanced matrix extensions. This limitation is reflected in a weak PassMark CPU encryption score of 1300.22 and poor LLM inference speeds, where text generation for a small 135M model reaches only 32.29 tokens/sec. However, the server maintains average performance in database operations and static web serving throughput. Given the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated physical cores, this instance provides a cost-efficient profile for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, and static web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is an ARM-based general-purpose server powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks local storage and GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks show average multi-core capabilities, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6000.0 and a static web serving throughput of 10.09 GB/sec. However, single-core performance and cryptographic operations are weak, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU encryption score of 1300.22 and the absence of AVX or AMX extensions. This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, and static web serving, offering a cost-efficient alternative to x86 architectures for workloads that do not require advanced vector instructions or local NVMe storage.
